text:
Omar (AE): quick heads-up — Orbit (enterprise fintech) wants a POC to replace VendorX. their big asks: prompt parity, response determinism for downstream scoring, and a security questionnaire for SOC2/ISO needs. asking for timeline + blockers.
Leah (Solutions Eng): got it. primary concerns: prompt/response deltas (tokens & format), embeddings drift, and rate-limit behavior. propose: 1) adapter shim to replicate VendorX params, 2) side-by-side eval harness with their prompt suite, 3) golden set for regression checks.
Ben (Product): +1. Also confirm if they need deterministic seeds or a deterministic model variant. We should offer quantized variant? pricing delta matters.
Eve (SRE): if they require deterministic outputs for scoring, we'll need pinned model versions and no temperature jitter. infra-wise, Dedicated pools make sense. can provide 99.9% SLA on reserved capacity.
Omar (AE): Orbit's security team already sent the questionnaire (SaaS + data residency). SecurityBot uploaded it here: https://files.redwood.example/secure/Orbit-SecQ-2026.pdf :lock:
SecurityBot: Security questionnaire uploaded by Omar. Link expires in 7 days.
Leah (Solutions Eng): for the adapter shim, here's a minimal example to map VendorX params -> Redwood API: 
```
// pseudo-config
vendorX: { model: x-3, temp: 0.0, top_k: 40 }
redwood: { model: redwood-v1-deterministic, temperature: 0.0, top_k: 40 }
// preserve stop sequences and response format (json_schema)
```
Leah (Solutions Eng): we'll run their prompt corpus (approx 1.2k prompts) through both systems and compute: token-level diffs, semantic-similarity (embedding cos sim), and response schema pass-rate. expect initial delta report in 3 business days.
Omar (AE): pricing question from Orbit: they want to understand TCO — hosted vs dedicated mixes. ask: what ranges should I give them for 100M tokens/month and 5M embed vectors?
Ben (Product): rough back-of-envelope: hosted (mixed models): $0.7k–$1.5k per 1M tokens depending on model, embeddings $0.01–$0.03 per vector. For 100M tokens that's $70k–$150k. Dedicated reserved capacity can drop unit cost ~30–50% depending on commit. I'll draft a formal quote after we know model choice.
Eve (SRE): list of enterprise blockers we should flag: 1) network egress policies for on-prem connectors, 2) KMS integration for key rotation, 3) audit log retention and SIEM hooks, 4) compatibility window for rolling deploys (can we support canary fallback to VendorX during early cutover?)
Leah (Solutions Eng): canary fallback requires proxying calls and normalizing responses. we can instrument header x-redwood-proxy to toggle shim mode. ops effort: ~2 engineers for a week to build & test.
Omar (AE): Orbit also asked about legal data residency (EU). They want region pinning and deletion guarantees.
SecurityBot: Note — Redwood Private supports region pinning (eu-west) and customer-managed KMS.
Leah (Solutions Eng): next steps: 1) run adapter shim + corpus eval (3d), 2) whiteboard canary design with SRE (2d), 3) hand off security Q to Security for answers (Eve). I'll post results in this thread.
Omar (AE): timeline works for Orbit. I'll schedule a demo for Wed. tagging @Leah @Eve for deliverables. :calendar:
Ben (Product): I'll prep a draft quote and a short TCO slide for Wednesday.
Eve (SRE): I'll start the security Q review today, expect initial answers by EOD tomorrow.
Leah (Solutions Eng): noted. prepping the eval harness now — will push a small repo and sample harness URL in thread in ~2 hours.
Omar (AE): thanks team — keep this thread for all deliverables. Orbit execs are on a tight window (legal review in 2 weeks).
Leah (Solutions Eng): ack.
Eve (SRE): ack.
Ben (Product): ack.
